title: StackAI Gives You a Team of AI Experts to Deploy Your Most Complex Use Cases
summary: StackAI pairs you with an AI strategist and forward-deployed engineer to deploy complex enterprise AI use cases and prove ROI.
body_markdown:
Simple AI is no longer where enterprises need help. General-purpose assistants like ChatGPT and Claude handle drafting, summarizing, and basic analysis well. The use cases that remain are the ones that decide whether AI delivers measurable value: custom integrations, on-premise data, and workflows governed by domain-specific rules.


StackAI pairs its enterprise agent platform with a[dedicated team of AI experts](https://www.stackai.com/platform/implementation?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=202610-white-glove-enterprise-global-awareness&utm_content=blog_post) built for that work. Every customer is supported by an AI strategist and a forward-deployed engineer who build complex use cases on the StackAI platform and get them into production during a structured three-to-six-month proof of value.


## Key Takeaways


-


General-purpose assistants handle simple tasks; StackAI's experts focus on complex enterprise use cases.


-


Every customer is paired with a dedicated AI strategist and forward-deployed engineer.


-


Before any contract, a 3–6 month proof of value puts three use cases in production, including custom integrations and on-premise deployments.


## Other AI Platforms Fall Short Where Enterprise Work Begins


Most AI platforms are built for work that needs little integration and little expertise: answering questions, summarizing documents, drafting a first pass. Enterprise work is harder on both counts. It runs through systems of record with no connector, databases that cannot leave the network, and secure processes only a few specialists fully understand.


That is where these platforms fall short. They provide a builder and documentation, then leave the customer to solve integration, security, and process design alone. The gaps surface months into a deployment, after the budget is committed.


StackAI starts from the opposite premise: complexity is the engagement. That is why the platform comes with a team of deployment experts designed to prove the value of every AI use case.


## Two AI Experts Dedicated to Every Customer


Every StackAI customer is paired with an AI strategist and a forward-deployed engineer. Together, they own the deployment from the first use case to measurable return on investment (ROI).


**The AI strategist** works with your teams to identify where agents will deliver the greatest return, across functions such as legal, finance, support, and compliance. Strategists define success metrics, track ROI, and refine live agents so the value of AI keeps compounding across the business.


**The forward-deployed engineer** turns those processes into production-grade agents. Engineers build the integrations each workflow requires, deploy on-premise when data cannot leave the network, and train your staff to maintain and extend what they build.


Both work in the channels your teams already use, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email, and join live calls over Google Meet or Zoom whenever a question needs a conversation.


## A Proof of Value That Ends With Agents in Production


On most no-code platforms, a trial means self-serve access. The customer builds, troubleshoots and makes the internal business case alone.


StackAI’s proof of value is a structured three-to-six-month engagement on the StackAI platform, led by the customer’s AI strategist and forward-deployed engineer. Customers come in with an objective, such as automating Excel-based processes or improving how teams work across existing tools. The StackAI team scopes, builds and deploys three use cases on the platform, running on the customer’s data and connected to its systems.


By the end, the customer has agents in production, measured ROI and a team trained to build the next use case on its own. This model has enabled StackAI to work with some of the most complex organizations in the world, where AI adoption takes strategy, process mapping and stakeholder alignment, not just a software download.


## Middlesex Federal Savings, From Pilot to Partner


Middlesex Federal Savings began with a three-month pilot in July 2025, scoped to its IT department and senior leadership. Early results led the bank to extend the pilot to six months and bring in more users. By January 2026, Middlesex had become a full customer.


Throughout the pilot, StackAI's implementation team met weekly with multiple departments to identify use cases, refine workflows, and accelerate adoption. Agents now support accounting, loan operations, platform innovation, and information security. Report automation that once took hours now runs in minutes, as do SOC 2 document reviews, alongside an internal policy chatbot and financial reconciliation agents. Multi-department adoption took less than a year.[Read the full story](https://www.stackai.com/customers/how-middlesex-federal-savings-drove-multi-department-ai-adoption-in-under-a-year) .


##### “StackAI's implementation team has been exceptional,” said Kosta Georgopoulos, VP of Information Technology, noting the team solved problems even outside scheduled touch points.


## Start With Your Most Complex Workflow


General-purpose AI has made simple automation widely available. The opportunity now lies in workflows that span disconnected systems and sensitive data. StackAI's AI experts are ready to take on the most demanding one first.
